text: Agricultural Guide: Essential Farming Practices 1. Crop Seasons: Kharif vs Rabi Agriculture in India is primarily divided into two main seasons: Kharif and Rabi. - Kharif Crops: These are monsoon crops, sown at the beginning of the rainy season (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October). Major Kharif crops include rice, maize, sorghum, and cotton. - Rabi Crops: These are winter crops, sown in the post-monsoon period (October-November) and harvested in spring (March-April). Major

Summer Crop Protection (30-45°C) Summer heat can severely stress crops. Effective protection strategies include: - Irrigation Timing: Irrigate during early morning or late evening to minimize water loss due to evaporation. - Mulching: Use organic mulch (like straw) to cover the soil surface, which helps retain moisture and regulate soil temperature. - Heat Stress

Monsoon Planting Advice The monsoon season provides the necessary hydration for many crops but brings challenges: - Drainage: Ensure proper field drainage to prevent waterlogging, which can cause root rot. - Fungal Diseases: Increased humidity can lead to fungal infections.
